statementIssues.note: The sentence 'In one reserve squad, players with no match time still accumulated about one match's worth of weekly high-speed and sprint distance, half that of 90-minute players' cites no surviving claim, and its source (library 473) is missing from `sources`. The drafter's verifier removed the C23 excerpt. The content is accurate to Casamichana et al. ('HSR and SPR weekly accumulation was double for the 90-min vs the 0-min group ... the 0-min group still reached ... one match'), so it is a traceability failure, not a misstatement.

The CI overlap, pooled no-difference, false-positive caveat, whole-squad-versus-substitutes turnaround split, and 'tailor the days before' content all come from claims C25, C26 and C36, which were removed. C14 and C37 do not support them. Every point checks out against Buchheit 2023 pp1061-1065, so this is a citation-hygiene problem, not a fidelity one.

'matched or exceeded team-training values' and 'well below match values' compare against literature-reported reference values (Picinini p6, p8), not the players' own teams. Peak speed was 82% of match, so 'well below' is slightly strong for that metric.
Says the authors state 'only small-sided games with few players (3v3 or 4v4) are effective'. The source says 'only some specific drills such as small-sided games with few players', citing ref 18.
'32% using GPS external load' cites no claim. It is accurate (survey table Q11: 20, 32.3%). The survey covers hamstring strain management only, which this sentence does not restate.

'efforts above 95% were too rare to show any relationship' goes beyond C22, which says only 'no relationship'. Shah p9 does support it: 'As the number of efforts at max>95% were so low, the findings regarding efforts > 95% are tentative'.

Athlete-reported readiness diverged from test scores in Askling, but the study did not validate self-report against reinjury or outcome. A short qualifier would stop readers treating it as a validated signal.
The pipeline moved a 'study that would change the answer' item into coverageGaps, where it reads as a duplicate gap rather than a whatCouldChange item.

tierNote: Limited is appropriate. The evidence is indirect: a case series, a single case, a small sprinter case series, a survey, and observational load studies in uninjured squads. None tests a 7-10 day end-stage plan or progress, hold or regress rules. recommendedDirection is null, and the actions are framed as options with plainly labeled professional judgment, so no recommendation is given at Limited.
usefulnessNote: A PT and performance staff pair gets a usable frame: close the deceleration and reactive-cutting gaps through partial team drills, place near-maximal speed exposures with caution, use a criteria panel rather than one cutoff, and name decision owners. Transferability limits and coverage gaps are stated honestly. It is dense and long for a two-minute read, and some action text is not traceable to cited claims.
suggestedDrafterFixes: When the verifier removes a claim, also remove or rewrite every statement sentence that depended on it, instead of only dropping the claimId; fail the brief if a statement sentence asserts a source finding that no surviving claim covers.
Require every source-attributed sentence in actions, monitoring and evidenceTension to map to a cited claim whose source is listed in `sources`.
When a study compares against literature reference values rather than the participants' own data, say so in the claim and the statement (for example, 'versus published team-training values').
Keep source hedges such as 'some specific drills such as' instead of turning them into 'only X'.
Route 'a study that would change this' items to whatCouldChange instead of coverageGaps, and cap action text length so the brief can be read in about two minutes.
